title: New Preference values do not update
body:
Defaults are only set once on first initialize. Not sure if this will cause weird issues (like #39?) or just give bad defaults.

This `IsEmpty` check should be removed and replaced with either;
1) Call `GetType()` on each element inside the loop
2) Outside the loop call `GetTypes()` (with an 's') for each type and check `if x in Type[]` inside the loop

title: Clockless nodes learn their announce timebase from any validated announce, so one crafted announce can poison it past the 40-bit field
body:
Follow-up to #155, whose fix (`4dcd3b4`) is otherwise sound. This is about the
clockless branch only; nodes with a real clock are unaffected because
`Clock::wall_unix_secs` always takes precedence.

## The gap

`Transport::learn_emission_timebase` (`leviculum-core/src/transport.rs:2577-2584`)
adopts the emission timestamp of any **validated** announce, with no upper
bound:

```rust
fn learn_emission_timebase(&mut self, emitted_secs: u64, now_ms: u64) {
    if self.clock.wall_unix_secs().is_some() {
        return;
    }
    if emitted_secs > self.emission_secs(now_ms) {
        self.emission_floor = Some((emitted_secs, now_ms));
    }
}
```

"Validated" means the announce's signature matches **its own** identity
(`announce.validate()` at `transport.rs:3295`). Anyone can generate an identity,
so any peer can put any value in that field and have it accepted. The call site
sits before the own-destination echo drop — correct for the restart case #155
solves, but it also means every announce from anywhere on the mesh is a
candidate source for our clock.

## Why it bites

The field is 5 bytes: `generate_random_hash` copies bytes 3..8 of
`emission_secs.to_be_bytes()` (`RANDOM_HASH_TIMESTAMP_OFFSET = 3`,
`RANDOM_HASH_TIMESTAMP_SIZE = 5`), and `emission_from_random_hash` reads them
back as a 40-bit big-endian value. So the representable maximum is
`2^40 - 1 = 1099511627775` (year 36812); real unix time is around `1.78e9`,
four orders of magnitude below.

An announce crafted with an emission near `2^40 - 1` therefore:

1. is accepted by a clockless node as its emission floor, permanently — the
   floor only ever moves forward;
2. makes that node's own announces carry an absurd timestamp, which every peer
   that stores the blob then carries in its path table (the same pollution #155
   documented: 660 of 10983 entries on one live rnsd);
3. and, once `emission_secs` grows past `2^40 - 1` via the monotonic advance,
   the copy silently truncates the high bits, so the emitted value **drops**.
   From that point the node cannot beat its own stored entries on any peer and
   cannot update its own paths — which is exactly the failure mode #155 was
   about, re-entered through a hostile input instead of through our own clock.

Step 3 needs no unusual timing: with a floor at `2^40 - 1` it happens on the
next announce.

The blast radius is the clockless platform — today the LNode — whose announce
inputs arrive over the air from anyone in range.

## Suggested direction

Not prescriptive, but the cheap options in rough order of preference:

- **Absolute sanity ceiling.** Refuse to learn a value above a constant well
  below `2^40` (a date decades out is still far below it). One comparison, no
  state, and it removes the truncation case entirely.
- **Bounded advance.** Once a floor exists, cap how far a single announce may
  move it forward (a day, say). A clockless node then converges on network time
  without any one peer being able to jump it.
- **Restrict the source.** Learn only from announces on an interface the
  operator marks trusted, or require corroboration from more than one
  destination before adopting a value.

Independently of which is chosen, `emission_secs` should never be able to return
a value that does not fit the 40-bit field — a saturating clamp at the point of
use would make the truncation unrepresentable rather than merely unlikely.

## Test

The existing clockless test
(`transport.rs::test_clockless_node_learns_emission_timebase_from_announce`) is
the right shape to extend: feed a validated announce carrying `2^40 - 1`, assert
the floor does not adopt it, and assert that a subsequent announce's emitted
value is still strictly greater than the previous one.

## See also (not part of this issue)

- The learned floor is not persisted (`emission_floor` is an in-memory
  `Option`), so after a reboot a clockless node emits uptime seconds again until
  it hears its first announce. `4dcd3b4`'s message compares the mechanism to
  microReticulum's *persisted* offset; ours does not persist.
- `set_wall_time_unix_secs` is exposed up to `NodeCore` but is not yet wired to
  the LNode serial config channel.
